_cross_session_note: The bell: every channel send and publish prints one line the session rings its peer session with, through Claude Code's cross-session messages. The bell carries no content - the channel log is the record and its hash the binding - so this project accepts inbound messages. A project value applies only when it is stricter than the user's or managed settings, so a person's own hold or refuse still wins.
_attribution_note: includeCoAuthoredBy is OFF by design: Claude Code's default appends a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude' trailer to every commit, and per-commit AI attribution is the user's call, not the tool's. The kit's stance: disclose the AI-assisted build ONCE, at the repo level (a README line, if the user wants it) — not on every commit. Delete this key to restore the upstream default.
_comment: Project-scoped Claude Code settings for the Build Framework. The SessionStart hook auto-loads the read-first orientation files at the start of every session in this repo. The hook is a Node.js script (Claude Code already requires Node, so no extra dependency) and is cross-platform: works on Windows cmd / PowerShell, macOS, Linux, and WSL without bash. The hook reads .claude/read-first-list.txt and obeys the read_first_cap setting in project-config.md.
_permissions_note: Permission fence (calibrated by approval_cadence). The dial that sets how often you review (Maximum / Standard / Minimum) ALSO drives this fence: one question, two effects. The three named profiles live in `_permission_profiles` below — BOOTSTRAP selects ONE at generation (Maximum approval -> maximum_oversight; Standard -> fenced_autonomy [recommended]; Minimum -> sleep_through), copies it into the live `permissions` block, and deletes `_permission_profiles`. The live block below ships the recommended default (fenced_autonomy). Precedence is deny > ask > allow; deny is the hard wall and wins from any scope. The DENY FLOOR IS IDENTICAL across all three profiles — the wall does not move; only the allow/ask split flexes. defaultMode acceptEdits removes file-edit prompts; read-only git (status/diff/log/show/branch) is already auto-approved so it is not listed. git commit/push are ASK on purpose to keep the framework's G1 'no commit without approval' gate alive even under acceptEdits or auto mode. The red-gate RELEASE commands (approve-red.cjs / stage-active.cjs) are ASK in every profile too (UAT #15 — the gated agent must never release its own gate unseen): under the Bash tool the agent's invocation always surfaces for approval, while the human's own outside shell never passes through this fence at all — deny would wrongly lock the human's in-session /approve-red path, so ask is the correct strength. The red-gate hook lets each script run only in its bare forms, which these ask rules always match under the Bash tool, and from a session the release, the void and the clear refuse unless the prompt the command asked is on record in the session's receipts (M34.6.G); the human's own terminal, outside the Claude Code session, runs them as before with no prompt, except under a test runner or a package script, or where the process tree cannot be read. The kit sets no ask rule for the PowerShell tool, which is on automatically on Windows without Git Bash, opt-in elsewhere with CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1, and off on Windows with Git Bash while these Bash deny rules stand, unless that variable is set; under it the hook refuses any command naming either script or one of its control files unless it is a bare form, and the recorded prompt still holds (deterministic enforcement, M34.6.J). BOOTSTRAP MUST replace the {{...}} placeholders with this project's real commands/manifest (e.g. {{TEST_CMD}} -> 'npm run test *'); until filled, those allow rules simply do not match (less convenient, not unsafe). SECRETS CAVEAT — be honest: deny Read() only blocks Claude's own file tools and recognized bash file commands (cat/head/tail/sed), NOT an arbitrary subprocess (a node/python script that opens the file itself). '.claudeignore' does NOT work. For real secrets use a secret manager / keep them off disk, and enable the sandbox for OS-level enforcement. THE RED GATE'S CONTROL SET (M33.A, M34.A): the Edit(/.claude/...) deny rules keep Claude's edit tools off the gate's own markers, the hooks and the local settings in every mode, outside a stage too, and Edit(/sbak/release-manifest.json) keeps them off the installed release manifest the hook authenticates the repair script against; they mirror scripts/lib/hook-root.cjs CONTROL_FILES plus CONTROL_PATHS settings.json included: Phase 3 fills a copy outside .claude/ and places it with node scripts/kit-update.cjs --place-settings <filled-file>, which checks the kit's hook registrations and permissions floor before it replaces the file (M34.C). Edit(/.claude/read-first-list*.txt) keeps them off the read-first lists the same way: a changed list is staged outside .claude/ and placed with node scripts/kit-update.cjs --place-read-first <role> <staged list>, which checks its shape before it replaces the list (M34.D). THE COMMIT FLOOR AND THE CHANNEL FILES (M34.5.F.1): Edit(/.claude/channel/...) keeps Claude's edit tools off the send token, the approval record, both channel logs and the watcher markers, which only the kit's scripts and hooks write; Edit(/.githooks/**), Edit(/validators/**) and the rules on the kit scripts the git hooks run keep them off the commit floor, which the kit's scripts change only through node scripts/kit-update.cjs --apply, --place-floor or the upgrade, and which the person may edit in their own editor (deterministic enforcement for the agent's tools; the person's edit is human authorization); these deny rules hold whatever else is on disk, and the red gate judges the same paths for shell writes in every state, the commit floor where sbak/release-manifest.json is installed, and under the PowerShell tool by the shell write gate's reading of the command (deterministic enforcement). --place-floor is an ask in every profile: the prompt on it is the person's (human authorization), and who is at the keyboard is the terminal check's, not this fence's. The pre-commit compares itself and each validator it runs with sbak/release-manifest.json before it runs any, and refuses a difference the file does not declare divergent, or validators set to warn where the tier requires them to block (deterministic enforcement); a severity change for G9 is the test_honesty row in the staged project-config.md, read at each commit (deterministic enforcement; the kit does not check who set it); for the other validators it is the person's edit of the hook line in their own editor under the pre-commit's ARC-007 divergence marker, which switches the self-check off for that file (human authorization). The limits that stay: a neutered pre-commit does not run its own check, so these two layers are what keep it whole; a program the agent writes and an allowed command runs is not judged by the hook (agent judgment); and the git fence asks for a commit and a push only, so git commands that rewrite the working tree are judged by the shell write gate's named forms alone. WHO IS AT THE KEYBOARD (M34.5.F.2): the release, the void, the clear and the release send decide whose call it is by the process tree, not by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID alone: a Claude Code process (or bwrap, its Linux sandbox runner, which Flatpak apps also run under) among the call's ancestors makes it a session's, and an empty session id there is refused; a test runner or a package script between the call and that process, or anywhere in the chain when there is none, is refused (deterministic enforcement); a process that leaves the tree reads as the person's own terminal, a script on the same account (the limit). The /send --approval token is minted by the UserPromptSubmit hook only while a release is pending and is taken only in the session and the turn that typed it, within ten minutes (the owner's typed word, recorded by the hook: human authorization). THE GIT FENCE (M34.5.F.2): the red gate parses every git command its shell write gate reads (not one inside a script file or from a variable) and answers ask for a commit or a push in every state, so in default mode and in auto mode, where Claude Code does not hand a hook's ask to its classifier, the call goes to the person's permission prompt (deterministic enforcement; the prompt is the person's; bypassPermissions was not tested), and the ask list also carries git -c, git -C and env before commit and push as text, the second layer. THE SECRET FILES' FAMILY (M34.5.F.1, R-260): Read(**/.env*) and Edit(**/.env*), with **/.netrc and **/.git-credentials, keep Claude's file tools off every .env file at any depth, .env.example included (deterministic enforcement); the earlier exception for the committed template is reversed, so the person keeps .env.example, or the agent drafts it under another name for the person to place (human authorization). Both red-gate registrations carry "onFailure": "block", so a red gate that cannot run blocks the call instead of letting it through; Claude Code reads the field from 2.1.295, the floor release-manifest.json pins and node scripts/kit-update.cjs --ready checks. Scripts (set-mode, stage-active, approve-red, kit-update) write these files; the agent never does. Edit rules cover every edit tool, so there is no Write(...) twin (Claude Code never consults one). The red-gate hook also judges the PowerShell tool; no PowerShell(...) rule is set, because Claude Code documents that on Windows with Git Bash installed, where a Bash deny rule turns that tool off, a scoped PowerShell rule keeps it on. AUTO MODE: a repo cannot set defaultMode:auto (ignored from project/local settings) — enable it in ~/.claude/settings.json for classifier-backed unattended runs; the deny floor below stays the hard backstop.
_high_risk_approval: Challenge-and-response on high-risk surfaces (the EU AI Act Art. 14 human-oversight control). The fence here is allow/ask/deny only — it CANNOT itself enforce a checklist, so it POINTS at the process artifact: for any RISK-TRIGGER surface (FRAMEWORK-CONFIG §4.19 — destructive data ops / archive-restore-extraction / untrusted-metadata FS writes / credentials / generated-untrusted-HTML / installers-updaters), the approver fills `HIGH-RISK-APPROVAL-CHECKLIST.md` (intent · data lineage · permissions chain · blast radius · rollback plan) BEFORE approving — a bare yes is not enough. This is ADDED rigor on high-stakes surfaces, NOT a replacement for the ask: git commit/push stay `ask` in every profile (G1), the deny floor still walls off secrets + irreversible Bash, and the four honest caveats (CLAUDE.md §6.5) still hold — the checklist closes the JUDGMENT gap, not a technical one. It does NOT fire for a change with no declared trigger (don't make a Lite project's checklist a doc typo).

maximum_oversight._for: approval_cadence: Maximum — tight leash; review most actions. Novice / sensitive / learning.

fenced_autonomy._for: approval_cadence: Standard — approve what you'd approve anyway; routine reversible work runs unattended. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT.

sleep_through._for: approval_cadence: Minimum — wake to finished work. Same repo-set allow/ask as fenced (auto can't be repo-set); pair with the USER-LEVEL `auto` opt-in documented in the generated CLAUDE.md. Trusted direction, long unattended runs.

_receipts_note: Build-receipt capture (M20.6.B). ONE shared lifecycle adapter, node .claude/hooks/receipts-lifecycle.cjs, is registered on every lifecycle boundary below (extend-not-fork). It is ADDED ALONGSIDE the SessionStart read-first hook and the UserPromptSubmit mode-check (a second command in the same group), and its PreToolUse entry is a NEW broad-matcher (.*) group BESIDE the edit-scoped red-gate (riding the red-gate matcher would drop tool_started for Bash/Read/Grep). EXIT-CODE DISCIPLINE (RCPT-09): the adapter has exactly one exit (0) and writes no stdout, so a metrics fault can never change a hook's exit (a Stop exit-2 forces continuation; a UserPromptSubmit exit-2 erases the prompt) — instrumentation failure surfaces as an incomplete interval, never a blocked session. Raw events go to .claude/receipts/ (gitignored); the privacy allowlist (scripts/lib/receipts.cjs) is the mechanism — no prompt text, no paths, no tool arguments, no tool names, ever.
